title: Retrieval Beyond Documents
subtitle: Capability Retrieval for Language Agents
description: RBD at NAACL 2027 explores capability retrieval for language agents: tools, skills, workflows, memory, models, and agents. Topics, submissions, and speakers.

topics.title: Representing and indexing capabilities
topics.description: Methods for describing and indexing tools, APIs, skills, workflows, memories, models, and agents using natural language, schemas, code, demonstrations, execution traces, graphs, ontologies, or embeddings. This includes indexes that change as capabilities are added or updated.

topics.title: Retrieval, routing, and composition
topics.description: Selecting individual capabilities or compatible combinations for a task. Topics include joint retrieval, dependencies between resources, and selection that accounts for permissions, reliability, and cost.

topics.title: Retrieval during agent execution
topics.description: Adapting retrieval to an agent’s state, plan, and observations. Topics include query reformulation, clarification, task decomposition, incorporating and invoking capabilities, delegation, replanning, recovery, and deciding when to abstain.

topics.title: Evaluating capability use
topics.description: Benchmarks and methods that distinguish errors in retrieval, incorporation, invocation, composition, and execution. Topics include whether a retrieved set contains all required capabilities, respects dependencies, and supports reliable task completion within resource constraints, as well as confidence calibration.

topics.title: Capability registries and deployment
topics.description: Dynamic and federated registries, access control, and Model Context Protocol ecosystems. Topics include provenance, permissions, keeping capability information current, monitoring system behavior, caching, reliability, and recovery.

speakers.name: Iryna Gurevych
speakers.bio: Iryna Gurevych is a Professor of Computer Science at TU Darmstadt and heads the Ubiquitous Knowledge Processing Lab. Her research spans natural language processing, semantic representations, information retrieval, and trustworthy AI. She studies how language technologies can work reliably with knowledge and support scientific research, with broader interests in generative AI, evaluation, and AI safety. She is an ACL Fellow and a past President of the Association for Computational Linguistics. Her honors include an ERC Advanced Grant and the Royal Society’s Milner Award and Lecture in 2025.

speakers.name: Graham Neubig
speakers.bio: Graham Neubig is an Associate Professor at Carnegie Mellon University’s Language Technologies Institute, where he leads NeuLab, and Chief Scientist at OpenHands. His research spans natural language processing and machine learning, including language models, multilingual communication, question answering, and code generation. He studies how AI agents can use tools, learn from experience, and carry out complex tasks, with a particular interest in software development. Alongside his research, he develops open source software and freely available courses and lectures that make advances in NLP accessible to researchers, students, and practitioners.

speakers.name: Scott Wen-tau Yih
speakers.bio: Scott Wen-tau Yih is a Research Scientist at Meta Fundamental AI Research. His research connects natural language processing, machine learning, and information retrieval, with a focus on neural search, question answering, and language models grounded in external knowledge. His recent interests include factuality in text and multimodal systems, retrieval augmented generation, and reasoning. Previously, he held research positions at the Allen Institute for AI and Microsoft Research. He is an ACL Fellow, has received paper awards at CoNLL and ACL, and served as a program co-chair of EMNLP 2021.

speakers.name: Jimmy Lin
speakers.bio: Jimmy Lin is a Professor and holds the David R. Cheriton Chair in the School of Computer Science at the University of Waterloo. He works at the intersection of information retrieval, natural language processing, and data management, developing systems that help people make sense of large collections of information. His research spans neural search, question answering, language models, and agentic retrieval, with a sustained emphasis on reproducibility and open source software. He is an ACM Fellow, an ACL Fellow, and a member of the SIGIR Academy.

organizers.name: Hitesh Laxmichand Patel
organizers.bio: Hitesh Laxmichand Patel is a Principal Applied Scientist and Tech Lead at Oracle. His research focuses on reliable AI agents, reasoning, and the use of external knowledge in language and vision models. He studies how agents gather information, interact with tools, and coordinate over extended tasks, alongside methods for training and evaluating multilingual and multimodal systems. His broader work addresses model alignment, safety, and robustness in practical applications. His research received the EMNLP 2025 Best Social Impact Paper Award. He co-organizes GRAIL-V at CVPR, serves in Area Chair roles, and contributes to open research communities.

organizers.name: Akari Asai
organizers.bio: Akari Asai is an Assistant Professor at Carnegie Mellon University and a Research Scientist at the Allen Institute for AI. Her research spans retrieval augmented and modular language models, adaptive retrieval, tools, and deep research agents, including recent reasoning aware retrieval work (Chen et al., 2026). She has organized workshops, tutorials, shared tasks, and competitions across major NLP/ML venues.

organizers.name: Omar Khattab
organizers.bio: Omar Khattab is an Assistant Professor and the TIBCO Founders’ Career Development Professor in MIT EECS. His research develops neural retrieval and reliable compositional language model systems. Recent work includes OBLIQ-Bench on latent and implicit retrieval needs (Tchuindjo et al., 2026). He has co-organized workshops on compound AI systems and late interaction retrieval.

organizers.name: Danqi Chen
organizers.bio: Danqi Chen is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at Princeton University, co-leads the Princeton NLP Group, and is an Associate Director of Princeton Language and Intelligence. Her research spans text understanding, knowledge representation, retrieval, reasoning, and QA. Recent work includes BRIGHT (Su et al., 2025) and long horizon agentic search (Yen et al., 2025). She received her Ph.D. from Stanford in 2018.

organizers.name: Zifei Wang
organizers.bio: Zifei Wang is affiliated with the IMA Product Center at Tencent. His research focuses on multimodal information retrieval, ranking, and routing for Large Language Model agents. His recent work covers areas such as skill retrieval and capabilities (Wang et al., 2026), as well as multimodal image and text retrieval.

organizers.name: Avi Sil
organizers.bio: Avi Sil is Senior Director of Applied Science at Oracle, where he leads teams developing AI agent technologies. His research spans RAG, agentic workflows, inference time methods, verification, and natural language to code systems. He has served the ACL community as area chair, track chair, and demonstration chair.

organizers.name: Sewon Min
organizers.bio: Sewon Min is an Assistant Professor in EECS at UC Berkeley and a Research Scientist at the Allen Institute for AI. Her research focuses on understanding and advancing large language models, including their adaptability, factuality, reasoning, and use of large text corpora. She has organized workshops and tutorials on retrieval based language models and foundation models.

organizers.name: Connor Shorten
organizers.bio: Connor Shorten is a Research Scientist at Weaviate. His research focuses on the intersection of AI and Database Systems. His most recent work on IRPAPERS compares text and image based retrieval and question answering systems.
